function: Maps uplink pilots directly to RIMSA phase shifts and digital precoder to maximize sum rate, bypassing explicit channel estimation; p. 5-6.
system: MISO TDD: BS with RIMSA (radiative RIS, 32x32 = 1024 elements, 128 RF chains), 3 single-antenna users; carrier frequency not stated; p. 4, 9.
method: Pre-trained GPT-2 (6 layers, attention/FFN frozen) with Conv1D-BiLSTM-attention front end, fine-tuned end-to-end with hybrid loss (channel MSE, sum rate, ZF norm); p. 6-9.
data_channel: Custom simulated Rician channel (LoS steering vector plus i.i.d. NLoS, path-loss exponent 3.2); 10,000 training, 2,000 validation, 5,000 test samples; p. 5, 9-10.
test_conditions: Users uniform in [20,30]x[20,30] m, 3 users, 15/20 dBm uplink/downlink power; sweeps of pilot length, power and 3-8 users; no unseen-condition test stated; p. 9-13.
baselines: Learned: DDPG-based DRL [34] and graph-attention GNN [30]; non-learned: random RIMSA configuration; BCD only timed (Table IV), not compared on rate; p. 10-12.
metrics: Sum data rate and max-min rate (bps/Hz), training time, inference latency, parameter counts; p. 11-13.
complexity: Table II: LLM 1.73 M trainable (84.78 M total) parameters, 2.6 h training, 20 ms inference, versus GNN and DRL; p. 11.
openness: none; no code or data link in the paper.
q1_support: p. 5: "the Rician fading channel model hk for the RIMSA-user k link"; custom Rician model with own path loss (p. 9, exponent 3.2); no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 14: "Extending the evaluation to more diverse conditions" is left as future work; not met: Figs. 9-12 (p. 12-13) sweep pilot length, power and user number, but the paper never states a model trained in one condition and tested in another.
q3_support: p. 10: "No optimization: RIMSA configurations are set randomly serve as the baseline"; learned baselines are "A deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) framework" [34] and a GAT-based GNN [30]; sum-rate comparison in Figs. 9-12 (p. 12-13).
q4_support: p. 11: "the largest total parameters as 84.78M, the actual trainable parameters 1.73M"; Table II also lists 2.6 h training time and 20 ms inference time.
q5_support: p. 10: "The training dataset and validation dataset respectively contain 10,000 and 2000 samples"; not met: the samples come from the authors' own simulator and the paper gives no link to code or data.
notes: ris=1 because the paper calls RIMSA "a novel radiative RIS architecture" (p. 1), although it is the BS antenna with RF chains, not a reflecting surface; area 3 because the output is the RIMSA phase matrix and digital precoder. Sample counts differ: p. 10 gives 10,000/2,000/5,000 and p. 11 gives 10,000/1,000/2,000. The metasurface phases V are phase-only and amplitude control sits in W (p. 6). Prototype photo (p. 4) is not used for results.
